title: 'Now I know': Abraham gave certain proof of his fear of God
source_text: XVI. Quum autem Deus dicit ad Abrahamum, Nunc cognovi quod timeas Deum, quia non pepercisti unigenito tuo filio propter me. Significare non vult se prius de Abrahami pietate dubitasse, neque Abrahamum ipsi fuisse satis cognitum; sed tantum Abrahamum, dum paratus fuit proprium filium, Deo jubente, immolare, sui erga Deum amoris & timoris, certum & indubitatum experimentum dedisse, & tale quo posset convinci, qui ea de re hactenus dubitasset, neque fuisset satis certus & persuasus.
pass_a_gloss: But when God says to Abraham, Now I know that thou fearest God, because thou hast not spared thine only begotten son for my sake. He does not mean to signify that he had before doubted of the piety of Abraham, or that Abraham had not been sufficiently known to him; but only that Abraham, while he was ready to sacrifice his own son, God commanding, gave a certain and undoubted proof of his love and fear towards God, and such by which he could be convinced, who had hitherto doubted of that matter, and had not been sufficiently certain and persuaded.
pass_b_english: When God says to Abraham, 'Now I know that you fear God, because you have not spared your only son for my sake,' he does not mean that he had previously doubted Abraham's godliness or had not known him well enough.

He means only that Abraham, by being ready at God's command to sacrifice his own son, gave a sure and unquestionable proof of his love and fear toward God. It was proof enough to convince anyone who had so far doubted the matter and had not been fully certain and persuaded of it.

choices.why: The standard English term for God's knowing in advance; 'foreknowledge' is kept throughout for praescientia, with 'foresee' for praevidere.
